title: shep community dog index
description: Editor-time courtesy schema for web/public/dogs.json. web/src/data/dogs.ts's validate() (wrapped by unwrap()) is the actual gate this mirrors; if the two ever disagree, the validator wins. "version" pins this document to the wrapper shape shep understands -- see dog_index.rs's own module doc for why a bare array is refused now.

version.description: The wrapper's own format version, not an entry's. Bump only alongside a shep release that understands the new shape.

name.description: The dog's own name, unique (case-insensitively) across the index. Displayed as "package (Name)".

package.description: The crate or repository name; the real identity, also unique across the index.

adopt_as.description: The name this dog expects to be adopted under: shep adopt <path> --name <adopt_as>.

description.description: One line describing what the dog does.

repo.description: HTTPS URL of the dog's repository, not just a domain or a profile page.

version.description: The exact crates.io version this index approves. shep installs this version and no other. A cargo row without one is listed but cannot be installed.

sha256.description: Hex sha256 of the prebuilt binary for each target triple. The download URL is built from the row, never stored: <repo>/releases/download/v<version>/<package>-<version>-<target>, plus .exe on Windows. The release workflow writes these; a target with no entry is built from source. Needs version.

permissions.description: Each permission the approved version declares, copied from the dog's manifest at that version. Absent means the index lists none, which is every row written before this field; an empty array means this version declares none. shep install prompts from the manifest the binary prints, not from this list.

name.description: The permission's name, such as "flock.read" or "events:sheep.".

required.description: Whether the dog cannot run without it.
